name: Grumman S-2 Tracker / C-1 Trader
summary: Grumman carrier anti-submarine airplane, now seen in the US mostly as turbine-powered aerial-firefighting tankers and as piston-engine warbirds.

wings: High, straight, constant-chord wing that folds on the original carrier airplane
Large nacelles on the wing leading edge
engines: Two engines: round radial cowls on the original or longer turboprop nacelles with three-blade propellers on the Marsh conversion
fuselage: Deep, bulky fuselage with a tailhook and a fat belly
Tricycle gear that retracts into the engine nacelles
Long boom behind the tail on ASW versions, or retardant doors on tanker conversions
tail: Horizontal tail mounted on the fuselage

tellTales: Twin engines on a high wing with a fat, deep fuselage and tailhook
Tricycle gear folding into the nacelles on a carrier-type airframe
Stubby body and a single tall tail with a long rear fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The A-26 is a sleek mid-wing bomber with a slim fuselage; the Tracker is a high-wing with a deep, fat fuselage.
The Albatross has a boat hull and wingtip floats; the Tracker has a conventional fuselage and gear.
The Beech 18 is a small twin-tail airplane with tailwheel gear; the Tracker is a much larger tricycle-gear airplane with a single tail.
The DC-3 is a low-wing airliner with tailwheel gear; the Tracker is a high-wing with tricycle gear.
